entities.summary: Roger of Howden (c. 1160 – 1201) was an English chronicler, diplomat, and head of the minster of Howden in the East Riding of Yorkshire. He served as the Chancellor of the Archbishopric of York and was a key advisor to King John. Roger of Howden played a crucial role in the reign of King John, including his involvement in the signing of the Magna Carta. His chronicles provide valuable insights into the politics and society of medieval England. The chronicler's work, known as the 'Hoveden', is a primary source for understanding the reign of King John and the early 13th century. Roger of Howden's legacy is marked by his contributions to the chronicle of the English monarchy, which he helped shape during a pivotal period in English history. His diplomatic skills and knowledge of international relations were instrumental in shaping the kingdom's foreign policy during the 12th century. The chronicler's work has been extensively studied by historians, providing a unique window into the politics, culture, and society of medieval England. Roger of Howden's significance extends beyond his role as a chronicler, as his work has had a lasting impact on our understanding of the reign of King John and the development of English monarchy.
